name: rb3ptr
listed_description: Red-Black tree. Exposes almost all implementation primitives, so can be used for scenarios like augmentation, multiple compatible ordering functions, and more.
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. The GitHub repo (3 commits, last 2020-01-14) holds only README.md, rb3ptr.c, rb3ptr.h and example.c; the README is one line pointing at the project page, and the sources contain no benchmark or speed text. The project page http://jstimpfle.de/projects/rb3ptr/rb3ptr.html is EGRESS_BLOCKED; a WebSearch snippet of it describes an intrusive 3-pointer red-black tree similar to the Linux kernel rbtree, with a flexible API and no allocation, and says nothing about speed. Two searches (rb3ptr versus std::map) found no third-party benchmark. Design claim only, and the guessed std::map baseline does not apply (intrusive C tree, not a std::map replacement).

name: retter
listed_description: Collection of hash functions, ciphers, tools, libraries and materials related to cryptography and security.
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. The listed page https://maciejczyzewski.github.io/retter is EGRESS_BLOCKED. The GitHub repo is a curated collection (public domain, 3 commits, about 119 stars) whose README has no performance metrics or baselines, and its owner marks libchaos as the main project. It is a collection of cryptography materials, not a concurrency queue or lock, so the guessed category and baseline do not apply.

name: ring_span lite
listed_description: A simplified implementation of Arthur O'Dwyer's ring_span implementation ie. a circular buffer view.
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. README (about 29 KB, read in full by grep for bench, perf, faster, slower, ns) and the repo tree (include/nonstd, example, test, cmake, script) contain no benchmark directory or timing numbers; it is a C++98-to-17 single-header std::ring_span backport (BSL-1.0, 170 stars) documented for API and feature coverage only. No web search was spent on a third-party ring_span versus std::deque shootout; none surfaced from the repo pages.

name: rpp
reason: No verifiable numeric comparison against a named baseline. The repo (MIT, about 219 stars) has only rpp, test, CMake and CI files, no bench directory, and the README lists 'Fast Compilation' and 'High Performance' as goals without numbers; it defers to the blog post https://thenumb.at/rpp/ (Oxidizing C++), which is EGRESS_BLOCKED. A WebSearch result summary of that post says it compares a mainstream C++17 project of about 100k lines (about 20 s optimized build, std::chrono include alone 75 percent of the compile invocation) with an rpp-based renderer of about 100k lines (under 3 s, base.h include under 200 ms on average). That is snippet text only, compares two different code bases rather than one task, and names no baseline facility or standard library, so no record was written. LEAD: retry from an environment that can open thenumb.at/rpp; a tier C compile-time record (baseline: libstdc++ or libc++ headers such as std::chrono) may be possible. The category guess (smart-pointers-and-refcount) is wrong; rpp is a whole STL replacement.

name: s2n
listed_description: C99 implementation of the TLS/SSL protocols, designed to be simple, small, fast and secure.
reason: No published numbers against a named baseline reachable. The repo is now aws/s2n-tls (Apache-2.0, about 4.8k stars); its README only says 'designed to be simple, small, fast'. It does contain a public Criterion harness, bindings/rust/standard/benchmarks (README opened, Cargo.toml opened), that benchmarks s2n-tls on AWS-LC against rustls (AWS-LC) and OpenSSL for handshake, throughput and resumption (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, secp256r1 and x25519, RSA and ECDSA, with and without mTLS), but neither its README nor docs/ nor the search results show any result numbers; the docs directory has no performance document. Three WebSearch queries found only rustls versus OpenSSL numbers and an AWS post-quantum hybrid TLS benchmark post that was not opened. LEAD: running the harness (cargo bench) would give a tier A record against OpenSSL, but nothing was built or run here. Guessed category (concurrency-queues-locks) is wrong; s2n is a TLS library.

name: sc
listed_description: Common libraries and data structures for C.
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. README says 'High performance and minimal memory usage' and sc_map is described as 'a very fast hashmap' with linear probing, but the repo (BSD-3-Clause per the GitHub page, about 2.6k stars) has no benchmark directory, the component READMEs (map, queue, array, string, heap, timer, buffer) contain no numbers, the issue search for 'benchmark' returns 0 results, and the perf component is only a perf_event_open() counter utility. Two searches found no third-party shootout that includes sc_map. Directional claim only.

name: SDS
listed_description: Simple Dynamic Strings; a library for handling strings in C.
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. The repo (BSD-2-Clause per the GitHub page, about 5.6k stars) holds sds.c, sds.h, sdsalloc.h, Makefile, Changelog and test helpers, with no benchmark file. The README says SDS 2 'may be slower with certain workloads' and argues better cache locality from a single allocation, but gives no numbers. Related PRs: #101 (SDS 2 changes) claims up to 10x speedup on 32-bit ARMv7 for sdsll2str by using int instead of long long, which compares against the previous SDS code, not std::string or another library, with no method stated; #16 (case-conversion tweak) was closed with no benchmark data. One WebSearch for SDS versus std::string append numbers found none. Directional claim only; also a C library, so std::string is not a like-for-like baseline.
